label: PF Backlog 619
title: Add project_id scoping to backlog_items (+ stages/attempts) so product/project data is directly scoped, not only via joins/JSON

brief.what_adds: Direct project_id columns (backlog_items, stages/attempts) so per-product data is queryable/scoped without JSON/join reliance
brief.problem: Product/project-scope data is not directly scoped in the DB (backlog_items lacks project_id; stages/attempts scope only via run)

objective: Add project_id scoping to backlog_items (+ stages/attempts) so product/project data is directly scoped, not only via joins/JSON
acceptance_criteria: backlog_items exposes first-class scope + project_id columns (indexed (scope, project_id)) so a project's items are directly queryable without JSON extraction.
stages and attempts expose a denormalized project_id (indexed) so a project's stages/attempts are directly queryable without joining runs.

The 0012_project_scope migration is reversible (paired up/down), idempotent under the runner, and backfills existing rows; go/migrate TestShippedMigrationsLoadAndPair passes and the down SQL executes cleanly.
edpdata.BacklogStore round-trips scope/project_id (integration test against Postgres passes) and reads COALESCE(project_id,'') so nullable rows scan safely.
out_of_scope: foreign keys (soft refs chosen per EDP-17 A.1/A.3)
approach: New migration 0012_project_scope.{up,down}.sql: ADD COLUMN scope/project_id to backlog_items (+index), project_id to stages/attempts (+index), backfilled from data->>'project' / runs.project_id / stages.project_id. Extend go/edpdata/backlog.go (BacklogItem Scope/ProjectID + Put/Get/List incl. COALESCE on read). Add new indexes to db_explain_check EXPECTED_INDEXES; note in EDP-17-SCHEMA.md. Soft refs (TEXT+index, no FK).
verification: migration applied to Postgres (db_bootstrap: applied 0012); columns + 3 indexes verified
go build/vet clean; edpdata integration test PASS (scope/project round-trip)
go/migrate load+pair test PASS; down SQL executes cleanly (rolled-back tx)
db-explain OK (10/10 indexes); precheck fast green except 3 PRE-EXISTING test_backlog_dod failures
risks: pre-existing test_backlog_dod failures unrelated; nullable project_id handled via COALESCE on read

analysis.implementation_strategy: Add nullable project_id column to backlog_items, stages, attempts; backfill from existing JSON/joins; make writes set project_id; extend /api/v1/projects/{project} and /api/v1/engineering/stages + /api/v1/pipeline/stages filters; enforce FK to projects. New component only if no existing store fits.
dependency_findings: REQUIRES: existing projects table with stable project key (unverified)
BLOCKS: BI-PF-1388 EPIC proportionality which needs direct project scoping
conflict_findings: core/adopt_project.py and core/cross_project_learning.py also touch project scoping — check concurrent edits
Multiple APIs (engineering+pipeline stages) duplicate stage endpoints — one migration for both
duplication_findings: BI-0081 covers backlog management API but not project_id column scoping
BI-PF-0434 fixed cross-project dedup write bug — related guardrails to respect
No equivalent schema-scoping work found in components
analysis.rationale: Direct relational scoping removes fragile JSON/join scoping, unblocks proportionality work, and is an additive MODIFY reusing existing project APIs and stage endpoints.
assumptions: projects table exists and is the canonical scope key
stages/attempts are separate tables with FKs to backlog_items
Migration tooling exists for additive column changes
risks: Backfill may mis-attribute legacy items lacking project linkage
Nullable column can go stale if some writers bypass update
Duplicate stage endpoints may diverge during migration
evidence: candidate components already reference project scoping patterns
missing_info: Backfill strategy for legacy rows with no derivable project_id
Decision: nullable vs NOT NULL after backfill
Whether stages/attempts are separate tables or embedded JSON

context_review.reason: All fields are the same restated sentence; no concrete files/schemas, migration or backfill approach, and no real justification beyond 'not only via joins/JSON'.

api_impact.reason: data-layer schema + store only; no HTTP surface change
